2024_185_8_b_wass_oven_quotes.paragraph: Quote request documents from the Troy School District Food Services Department, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48198, solicit pricing for two electric UNOX combi ovens configured as one double stack for Wass Elementary School. The packet contains a completed REBID form and a blank copy of the original quote request. Great Lakes Hotel Supply of Southfield submitted a bid of $36,457.91 for Item 1, signed by contact Michael Trombley. Bids were to include all freight, delivery to the school, installation by an authorized service agent, and any utility rebates.
2024_185_8_b_wass_oven_quotes.page:
Overview
Two versions of a Food Services quote request for Wass Elementary School are included: a completed "REBID" form carrying a submitted price, and a blank original form. Both were issued by Troy School District, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48198, Food Services Department, and both are footed "Page 2 - Troy School Foodservice Bid - Wass Elementary."

Item 1 - Combi Oven, Electric (2 Ovens - One Double Stack)
Model specified is UNOX USA XAVC-06FS-EPRM, a ChefTop MIND.Maps Plus countertop electric combi oven. Dimensions are 33.13 (h) x 33.88 (w) x 38.06 (d). Capacity is (6) 18 x 26 inch full size sheet pans or (12) hotel size pans, with 2-11/16 inch shelf spacing. Features listed include MIND.Maps technology, programmable menu, glass door, right-to-left door opening, stainless steel interior and exterior, 316L stainless steel cooking chamber, water line included for a water connection within 3 feet, WIFI/USB data transfer to HACCP software, and cMETus, NSF and ENERGY STAR listings.

Line Items Requested

| Qty | Item |
| --- | --- |
| 1 ea | End User Data & Installation Confirmation Form |
| 1 ea | 2 year parts and 1 year labor warranty standard |
| 1 ea | LONG.LIFE4-B1 extended warranty with certified installation |
| 1 ea | LONG.LIFE4-B2 extended warranty with certified installation for 2nd oven |
| 2 ea | 208v/60/3-ph, 42 amps, 14.5 kW, no cord and plug (dealer to verify prior to ordering) |
| 2 ea | UNOX Power Cable, 3 Phase 6 AWG, NEMA 15-60 |
| 1 ea | Stacking kit including floor stand XWARC-00-EF-F and casters XUC012 |
| 1 ea | Ventless hood, 33-7/8 x 45-1/16 x 9-7/16, 4-3/4 inch chimney, 0.1 kW, 208-240v/60/1-ph |
| 1 ea | Ventless hood installation |
| 2 ea | Owner water-testing responsibility acknowledgment |
| 2 ea | UNOX.Finest Filtering System |
| 2 ea | Water filter installation |
| 1 ea | UNOX Detergent & Rinse Eco, (10) 1 liter tanks |
| 10 ea | CHROMO.GRID, 18 x 26 inch, stainless steel |
| 10 ea | "STEAM&FRY" basket, 18 x 26 inch, stainless steel |

Warranty Terms
The blank original form spells out the LONG.LIFE4 program: pricing based on a 100 mile radius from the installer, a 4 year/10,000 ON hours parts and 1 year labor extended warranty, a requirement that the oven remain internet-connected via Ethernet or WIFI and accessible for remote login by UNOX, a pre-installation site inspection by an UNOX Certified Service Agent, follow-up site preparation instructions, and assembly, setting, leveling and final hook-up by a Certified UNOX Service Agent.

Bid Received
Bid for item #1: $36,457.91. Business Name: Great Lakes Hotel Supply. Address: 24101 W. Nine Mile Rd., Southfield, MI 48033. Phone: (248) 982-7283. Contact and signer: Michael Trombley.

Submission
The REBID form directs returns by e-mail or by 5:00 p.m., Friday April 26th, 2024, to Gayle Moran, gmoran2@troy.k12.mi.us. The blank original form carries a due date of 5:00 p.m., Friday April 12th, 2024, to the same recipient. Bids are to include all freight charges with the dealer delivering to the school, installation by an authorized service agent, and any utility rebates.
2024_185_8_b_wass_oven_quotes.verbose:
Board packet material for agenda item 8.B., presented to the Troy Board of Education for the May 21, 2024 meeting, consists of foodservice equipment quote request forms for Wass Elementary School. The packet holds two versions of the same document: a completed form headed "Quote Request - Wass Elementary - REBID" bearing a submitted price and bidder signature, and a second, blank form headed "Quote Request - Wass Elementary" with the pricing and bidder fields left open. Both are issued under Troy School District, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48198, Food Services Department, and both carry the footer "Page 2 - Troy School Foodservice Bid - Wass Elementary."

Scope of the Request
The forms request a price for a single line, ITEM 1 - COMBI OVEN, ELECTRIC (2 Ovens - One Double Stack). The specified unit is UNOX USA Model XAVC-06FS-EPRM, described as a ChefTop MIND.Maps Plus Combi Oven, electric, countertop. Dimensions are given as 33.13 (h) x 33.88 (w) x 38.06 (d). Pan capacity is (6) 18 inch by 26 inch full size sheet pans or (12) hotel size pans. Additional specifications listed are MIND.Maps technology, programmable menu, 2-11/16 inch shelf spacing, glass door, right-to-left door opening, stainless steel interior and exterior, a 316L stainless steel cooking chamber, water line included for water connection within 3 feet, WIFI/USB for data transfer to HACCP software, and cMETus, NSF and ENERGY STAR designations.

Itemized Components
The bill of materials on both forms is identical. It comprises: 1 ea End User Data & Installation Confirmation Form; 1 ea 2 Year parts and 1 year labor warranty standard; 1 ea LONG.LIFE4-B1 extended warranty with certified installation; 1 ea LONG.LIFE4-B2 extended warranty with certified installation for the 2nd oven; 2 ea electrical configuration at 208v/60/3-ph, 42 amps, 14.5 kW, no cord and plug, with the dealer to verify prior to ordering; 2 ea UNOX Power Cable, 3 Phase 6 AWG, NEMA 15-60, for XAVC-06FS-EpxM and XAVC-1011-EPxM; and 1 ea Stacking Kit for ChefTop MIND.Maps Plus, which includes installation kits and stacking parts for stacking two ovens, for electric ovens, including floor stand XWARC-00-EF-F and casters XUC012.

Ventilation and Water Treatment
The request includes 1 ea Ventless Hood for ChefTop MIND.Maps Plus, dimensioned (WxDxH) 33-7/8 inches by 45-1/16 inches by 9-7/16 inches, with a 4-3/4 inch exhaust chimney diameter, including (1) 1-1/2 m hose and (2) hose clamps, rated 0.1 kW, 208-240v/60/1-ph, for models EPR and XAVC-06FS-EPLM, UL and NSF listed. The hood note states that it "reduces smoke, odors, grease latent vapors and lowers exhaust temperatures. Does not replace Type II exhaust hoods. Adhere to local codes." Also included is 1 ea ventless hood installation, which must be purchased with the corresponding unit LONG.Life4 and installed at the same time as the unit.

Two water-related acknowledgments are listed at 2 ea, placing sole responsibility on the owner, operator or purchaser to verify that the incoming water supply is comprehensively tested for Free Chlorine, Chloramine, TDS (Total Dissolved Solids), Silica, pH, TH (Total Hardness), Chlorides and Alkalinity, and if required to provide water treatment meeting the manufacturer's minimum water quality standards as outlined on the product spec sheet; non-compliance is stated to potentially damage the equipment or components and to VOID the original equipment manufacturer's warranty. The request further includes 2 ea UNOX.Finest Filtering System, which reduces carbonate hardness of water, with ChefTouch monitoring water consumption and notifying the user to replace the cartridge, and 2 ea water filter installation.

Consumables and Accessories
Listed are 1 ea UNOX Detergent & Rinse Eco, (10) 1 liter tanks, double concentrate, phosphate free, cleaning chemicals for Rotor.Klean; 10 ea CHROMO.GRID, 18 inch by 26 inch, stainless steel; and 10 ea "STEAM&FRY" Basket, 18 inch by 26 inch, stainless steel.

Extended Warranty Detail
The blank original form carries an expanded description of the LONG.LIFE4-B1 line. Pricing is based on a 100 mile radius from the installer, with additional charges possibly applying. The UNOX Long.Life4 program, subject to UNOX, Inc. terms and conditions, includes: (1) an extended warranty providing a 4 year/10,000 ON hours parts and 1 year labor warranty, with the oven required to be connected to the internet via Ethernet cable or WIFI and to remain accessible for remote login by UNOX; and (2) a pre-installation site inspection by an UNOX Certified Service Agent of the installation site, follow-up instructions advising the customer of any additional material needed for site preparation prior to installation, and assembly, setting and leveling of the UNOX equipment plus final hook-up by a Certified UNOX Service Agent. This applies to the 1st 06FS. LONG.LIFE4-B2 covers the extended warranty with certified installation for a 2nd or more unit(s) installed at the same time and location as the 1st unit (06FS).

Bid Conditions
Both forms state that the bid is to include all freight charges with the dealer delivering to the school, that installation by an authorized service agent is to be included, and that any utility rebates are to be included in the bid.

Bid Submitted
On the REBID form, the entry for "Bid for item #1" is $36,457.91. Bidder information given is Business Name: Great Lakes Hotel Supply; Address: 24101 W. Nine Mile Rd., Southfield, MI 48033; Phone: (248) 982-7283; Contact: Michael Trombley; Bidder's Signature: Michael Trombley. The blank companion form leaves the bid amount, business name, address, phone, contact and signature lines empty.

Deadlines and Contact
The REBID form instructs bidders to return the quote via e-mail or by 5:00 p.m., Friday April 26th, 2024, to Gayle Moran at gmoran2@troy.k12.mi.us. The blank original form gives the earlier deadline of 5:00 p.m., Friday April 12th, 2024, to the same contact, indicating the solicitation was reissued as a rebid with a later return date.

2024_187_m031924bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of a Troy Board of Education meeting held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, headed March 19, 2024, and carried on the April 16, 2024 agenda, record recognitions, public comment, and a series of unanimous 7-0 construction and technology awards. The Board certified an Operating Millage Renewal Proposal to the Oakland County Clerk for the August 6, 2024 election, with certification required no later than 4:00 p.m. on May 14, 2024. The largest action was the Smith Middle School foundations and steel contract package totaling $9,134,583.10 from the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. before roughly 300 audience members, and it adjourned at 9:51 p.m.
2024_187_m031924bdmtg.page:
Meeting and Attendance
Held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. Board members present with him were Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson. Superintendent Machesky attended along with administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, DiPonio, Zawislak, Henning, Bush, Recker, Jansen, Pagel, Fulcher and West. Approximately 300 members of the audience were present. Mr. Schmidt changed the order of Recognition items to allow additional time for guests to arrive for the Mission Moment. The meeting adjourned at 9:51 p.m. Minutes were submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

Recognitions
Larson Middle School received the 2024 State School of Character Award from Character.org, the only school in Michigan and one of only 87 schools in the country to earn it; it is Larson's third such recognition, following 2018 and 2019, and Larson may now apply for a National School of Character Award. Boulan Park instrumental music teacher Joe Havrilla presented 30 TSD musicians selected for the 2024 Michigan All-State Ensembles from four middle schools and three high schools, with 8 additional students named Honorable Mention; the students rehearsed and performed in Grand Rapids January 25-27. The Student Spotlight featured Troy High School senior Simmi Sharma of the TSD Creative Guild, introduced by Thomas Butcher. The Mission Moment honored winners of the Oakland County Water Resources Commission Kids' Clean Water Calendar Contest, drawn from nearly 600 county entries.

Consent Agenda and Personnel
Items A through D passed 7-0: minutes of the February 6, 2024 Workshop; minutes of the February 27, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report - January 2024; and a Retention Pond Budget Modification. Personnel recommendations (Bryan Wietecha) passed 7-0. The Board issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Matt Jansen as Director, Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment, effective July 1, 2024, by a 7-0 vote. Curriculum: none.

Business Actions

| Item | Award | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wattles abatement | Midwest Environmental | $36,500.00 | Building and Site Sinking Fund |
| Smith MS foundations | Simone Construction Services | $3,032,100.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Smith MS structural steel | B & A Structural Steel LLC | $4,838,848.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Site demolition and SESC | Blaze Contracting, Inc. | $587,000.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Smith MS bid total | | $8,457,948.00 | |
| Smith MS contingency | | $676,635.00 | |
| Smith MS TOTAL | | $9,134,583.10 | |
| Temporary fencing | Fence Connection | $51,036.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Cellular WAN (Cisco switches, Forti-Extender router, accessories) | People Driven Technologies | $790,132.15 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| 2024 furniture package | Pre-existing bid consortium contracts | not to exceed $4,828,873.07 | 2023 Bond Fund |

Non-Homestead Renewal
A Resolution Certifying Operating Millage Renewal Proposal was adopted 7-0, certifying the Proposal (Exhibit A) to the Oakland County Clerk as School District Election Coordinator for the election of August 6, 2024, with filing required no later than 4:00 p.m. on May 14, 2024, and authorizing updates for any Headlee rollbacks applicable to the 2024 operating millage.

Public Comment and Reports
Agenda-item speakers addressed Honors courses and the New Solutions K-12 study. Non-agenda comment centered on restroom use and transgender student policy and on the expired teacher contract, with Troy Education Association president Jason Cichowicz among the speakers. President Schmidt reported on a Lansing trip with Dr. Machesky and David Randels of Oakland Schools regarding Governor Whitmer's proposed school funding budget, and Dr. Machesky summarized the New Solutions K12 report.
2024_187_m031924bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the Troy Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, headed "BOARD MEETING MINUTES MARCH 19, 2024," held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The document appears in the April 16, 2024 board packet, and its embedded certification by Secretary Gary Hauff attests that the millage resolution was adopted at a regular meeting held on April 16, 2024, conducted in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. The minutes carry the typing notation GH/jh and are respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

Call to Order and Attendance
President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, DiPonio, Zawislak, Henning, Bush, Recker, Jansen, Pagel, Fulcher and West. There were approximately 300 members of the audience. Mr. Schmidt changed the order of Recognition items to allow additional time for guests to arrive for the Mission Moment.

Recognition: State School of Character
Larson Middle School was honored for receiving the State School of Character Award. Character.org certifies schools and districts that have developed and implemented an intentional, proactive and comprehensive approach embedding character into all aspects of school life, including creating a caring school community, providing students opportunities to practice and reflect on character strengths, and engaging families and communities as partners. Larson was the only school in Michigan and one of only 87 schools in the country to earn the 2024 State School of Character Award, its third such recognition after 2018 and 2019, and it has now earned the right to apply for a National School of Character Award. Character Committee leaders Charlie Tull, Jen Rogers, Jackie Parker, Shannon Dziwanowski and Cindy Christianson, along with school administrators Brian Zawislak and Stephan Henning, were brought up to receive congratulations.

Recognition: All-State Band and Orchestra
Boulan Park instrumental music teacher Joe Havrilla spoke about the 30 Troy School District musicians chosen as members of the 2024 Michigan All-State Ensembles, representing each of TSD's four middle schools and three high schools. Additionally, 8 students were recognized as Honorable Mention. The students were in Grand Rapids January 25-27 to rehearse and perform with musicians from across the state. Michigan High School All-State Orchestra members recognized were Karen Jin (violin), Ryeo-Won Kim (violin), Jing Yi Ma (viola), Benjamin Sheng (viola), Emily Baek (cello), Jisoo Park (cello) and Danielle Leight (bass). Michigan High School All-State Band members were Halle Chen (oboe), Jay Shyn (clarinet), Angela Park (clarinet), Sahana Mukund (bass clarinet), Brian Feng (alto saxophone), Daniel Lee (alto saxophone), Sohum Kapoor (trumpet), Brian Liu (trombone), Sarbani Sengupta (trombone) and Brandon Mendoza (percussion). Michigan Middle School All-State Orchestra members were Chole Kim (violin), Sihyeon Jun (violin), Gabriella Murphy (violin), Suhana Reddy (violin), Ariel Song (violin), Brian Zhang (violin) and Leon Ma (cello). Michigan Middle School All-State Band members were Andy Zhao (clarinet), Aryan Khedkar (bass clarinet), Anson Pingree (alto saxophone), Pujah Raj (alto saxophone), Tanishi Swami (alto saxophone) and Landon Taylor (French horn).

Student Spotlight and Mission Moment
The Student Spotlight recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild, showcasing Troy High School senior Simmi Sharma for her video projects, editing and video production; Thomas Butcher introduced her work. The TSD Mission Moment honored Clean Water Calendar winners for 2024. Students at Barnard, Costello, Hamilton and Leonard Elementary Schools participated in the annual Kids' Clean Water Calendar Contest sponsored by the Oakland County Water Resources Commission, tied to the first unit in Michigan Studies on the Great Lakes ecosystem. There were nearly 600 entries in the county. Grand Prize Winner was Sally Huang, Leonard 5th grade, for "Save Life, Save Water, Save Nature." Calendar Winners were Matthews Baheena, Costello 5th grade, "Saying Doesn't Help...Doing Does"; Rishik Palla, Costello 5th grade, "No More Pollution"; and Samrath Singh, Barnard 4th grade, "Keep Our Lakes Clean, Please." Honorable Mentions were Erin Abraham (Barnard 5th grade), Mihith Arun (Barnard 4th grade), Emanuela Ivezaj (Barnard 4th grade), Nandini Sinha (Costello 5th grade) and Zidaan Akhtar (Hamilton 5th grade).

Additions and Deletions; Public Communication on Agenda Items
Additions and deletions: none. Alex Karpowitsch, Troy resident and Troy High graduate, addressed the Board about Honors courses and how the change will impact students, adding that the District has not shared the data. Dr. Audra Melton addressed the Board about the New Solutions K-12 study and its recommendations related to reading programs and expanding elementary reading specialists. Mrs. Stephanie Zendler, a former 12-year TSD administrator, addressed the Board about the Levinson report discussed at the recent Board workshop, speaking on the special education program, Reading Recovery, and Fountas and Pinnell Literacy.

Consent Agenda
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board approved items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda: Minutes of the February 6, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the February 27, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - January 2024; and Retention Pond Budget Modification. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

Personnel
Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board approved the personnel recommendations as stated (Bryan Wietecha). Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Dr. Wilson, the Board issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Matt Jansen, who will begin duties as Director, Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment as of July 1, 2024. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Curriculum: none.

Business: Non-Homestead Renewal
A Resolution Certifying Operating Millage Renewal Proposal was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne. The recitals state that the Board determined it necessary for the continuing operation of the School District to renew the authority to levy certain operating mills as described in the Operating Millage Renewal Proposal attached as Exhibit A; that it is necessary and desirable to submit the Proposal to the School District's electors at an election to be held on August 6, 2024 (the August Election Date); and that the Board must certify the Proposal to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, State of Michigan (the School District Election Coordinator) as required by Michigan election laws not later than 4:00 p.m. on May 14, 2024. The operative provisions certify Exhibit A to the School District Election Coordinator and local clerks; individually authorize the Secretary of the Board and the Superintendent to file the Resolution and complete required forms, certificates or documents by no later than 4:00 p.m. on May 14, 2024; authorize the Secretary or Superintendent to update the Proposal prior to submission to reflect any Headlee rollbacks applicable to the current operating millage for the 2024 year; direct the Election Coordinator to post and publish notice of the last day of registration and notice of election and to have ballots prepared and printed in the form of Exhibit A or stated as a proposal on the voting machines, possibly alongside other matters presented to the electorate the same date; and rescind conflicting resolutions. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED, certified by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education.

Business: Contract Awards
Wattles Abatement - moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mr. Haupt: the bid for asbestos abatement awarded to Midwest Environmental in the amount of $36,500.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

New Smith MS Foundations and Steel - moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mr. Hauff: contract awarded as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund, with Foundations to Simone Construction Services at $3,032,100.00; Structural Steel to B & A Structural Steel LLC at $4,838,848.00; and Site Demolition and SESC to Blaze Contracting, Inc. at $587,000.00, for a Bid Total of $8,457,948.00, Contingency of $676,635.00, and a TOTAL of $9,134,583.10. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

New Smith MS Temporary Fencing - moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mrs. Alic: the bid for temporary fencing awarded to Fence Connection in the amount of $51,036.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

Cellular WAN - moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mr. Haupt: purchase of Cisco switches, Forti-Extender router and accessories awarded to People Driven Technologies in the amount of $790,132.15, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

2024 Furniture Package K-5 Classrooms, Baker, and IAE Classrooms - moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Dr. Wilson: furniture purchase for Costello, Hamilton, Leonard, Schroeder, Wass and Wattles elementary schools along with Baker Middle School and IA-East, for an amount not to exceed $4,828,873.07 through pre-existing bid contracts (consortiums) as outlined in the memo from TMP dated March 15, 2024, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

Student Representatives
Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events and activities at her school. Teagan Pruitt, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, was not in attendance. Jayla Turner, student representative for Troy High School, reported on her school. Mackenzie Sawyers filled in as Athens High School student representative since Marlien William was not in attendance and shared a report on Athens.

Public Communication, Non-Agenda Items
Mr. Peter Dungjen, a district parent, addressed a male student using the female restroom and the safety of all students. Mrs. Katie MacFarland, a district parent, supported Mr. Dungjen's daughter and asked the Board to invest bond monies in single stall bathrooms. Ms. Michelle Fox-Phillips, a Warren resident, spoke in support of transgender students using the restroom they choose and cited bullying and outing. Mr. Jason Cichowicz, Troy Education Association president, addressed the expired teacher contract, fair and equitable compensation, and retaining teachers. Ms. Justine Galbraith, a district teacher, spoke on upholding gender identity and student safety. Yvonne Tadajewski, P-Flag president of the Clinton Township Chapter, spoke in support of transgender students. Mrs. Emily Freeman, a district teacher, addressed the expired contract and the anxiety accompanying it. Kylie Wood, a district teacher, addressed the expired contract and teachers' need to be recognized and valued. Jennifer Smith, speaking on behalf of a non-tenured district teacher, addressed the expired contract, teacher burnout, and teachers working second jobs. Mrs. Jennifer Taylor, a district teacher, spoke on the expired contract and fair and equitable compensation. Ms. Audrey Carra, a first year district teacher, spoke on the expired contract and balancing work and life with student loan debt. Mr. Ollie Apahidean, a district parent, raised the restroom issue and pornography in the media center. Chris Kus, a district parent, raised the ongoing safety issue of a girl being bullied over the restroom issue and the removal of honors classes. Salwan Rabban, a Troy resident, addressed the female student bathroom being used by a male transgender student while stating respect for their choice and concern for student safety.

Other: Public Education Funding and NSK12 Levinson Report
President Schmidt reported that he, Dr. Machesky and David Randels from Oakland Schools traveled to Lansing the prior Friday to meet with the state senate appropriations committee chair about Governor Whitmer's proposed budget for public school funding. He shared a graph of per-pupil funding over the last 20 years showing that funding has not met the rate of inflation, expressed frustration at not getting the funding needed to support staff income, and said he will continue to push legislators to go beyond the governor's proposed PreK-12 budget. Dr. Machesky summarized the New Solutions K12 report, which would be available for public review on the TSD website, describing district challenges and values, the engagement of Mr. Levinson from NSK-12 to meet with stakeholders and gather data, the availability of data on MI-School Data via the transparency report on the TSD website, best practice professional development, a common understanding of MTSS across the organization, opportunities identified from the study and how to prioritize the work, the Guiding Coalition of stakeholders planning to meet quarterly, and review of student data at all levels to improve the achievement gap. Dr. Machesky and Board members shared about participating in district events, gave a shout out to volunteers who created sets for the spring high school plays, noted March is Reading Month and encouraged sign-ups to read to classrooms, and wished the TSD community a meaningful Ramadan, Happy Easter, Happy Holi and a Happy Spring Break. Mr. Schmidt spoke further about his Lansing trip and his conversation with the legislator about school funding.

Adjournment
The meeting adjourned at 9:51 p.m.
